clue.text: TV interference once broadcast goes over western tip of Norway

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece going over another covers it on both sides, so it encloses the letter

parts.note: to broadcast seed is to sow it, scattering it by hand

indicators.note: the western end of a word is its first letter, as words read west to east

explanation.surface: A complaint about a TV signal fault that stretches over to the far west of Norway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes over' puts N, the first letter of Norway, inside SOW.
explanation.definitionFit: Analogue television pictures used to break up into a speckled white haze called snow, a fault now mostly gone.

clue.text: Woe is me going round on reduced public transport

indicators.note: something going round is turning about, so the two short words are mixed up

parts.note: railway, a form of public transport, cut short to its abbreviation Ry

explanation.surface: A grumble that it is the speaker who must go the long way round because public transport was cut back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' gives MISE; in a down clue 'on' means placed above. Stephen King wrote a novel of this name, part of the puzzle's author theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Woe and misery are synonyms, both meaning deep unhappiness or distress.

clue.text: With hot drinks, listen out for the largest fish

parts.note: H is the usual abbreviation for hot, as on taps
ales are drinks served in a pub
hark is an old word meaning listen

explanation.surface: Advice to sit with hot drinks and keep an ear open for the biggest fish in the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The whale shark is the largest living species of fish, a huge plankton feeder of warm seas.

clue.text: Underwear? We may well have seconds

definitions.meaning: loose shorts worn as men's pants
fighters in the ring, each of whom has seconds attending in the corner

explanation.definitionFit: Boxers are both loose-fitting men's shorts and fighters in a ring, whose helpers are called seconds.

clue.text: Cure soft-spun sugar

indicators.note: letters that are spun are whirled round into a new order

explanation.surface: A cure for something made of spun sugar, like candyfloss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spun' rearranges CURE SOFT.
explanation.definitionFit: Fructose is fruit sugar, a simple sugar found in fruit and honey.

clue.text: Open a ruler up

indicators.note: in a down clue, reading up means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: a raj is a ruler or rule, as in British India

explanation.surface: An instruction to open up a ruler, as if unfolding a measuring rule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns RAJ into JAR, written under A.
explanation.definitionFit: A door that is slightly open is described as ajar.

clue.text: Revolution Road's dedicated track

parts.note: a cycle is one revolution, one full turn round
a way is a road, as in a street name

explanation.surface: A road called Revolution Road has its own special track.
explanation.definitionFit: A cycleway is a path set aside for bicycles, a track kept for one use.

clue.text: Nose blocked, eyes streaming? In that case, wear a hat!

definitions.meaning: the symptoms of a common ... in the ...

definitions.text: In that case, wear a hat!
definitions.meaning: read literally, a ... that is chilly, which a hat would warm

explanation.definitionFit: A head cold is a common cold felt in the nose and eyes; read literally the words also mean a chilly scalp.

clue.text: Be rough in breaking one who's close to you

indicators.note: breaking the words up and putting them together again in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is being rough while breaking in, perhaps a burglar or a horse trainer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' rearranges BE ROUGH IN; 'in' looks like a link word but it is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A neighbour lives close by, next door or nearby.

clue.text: Awfully coy at heart, "Jane without a name" gets a name

indicators.note: the mixed-up letters sit at the heart, the middle, of what remains of the girl's name
Jane going without letters means those letters are dropped from it

parts.note: A plus N, the usual abbreviation for name

indicators.note: awfully suggests something badly done, so the letters of coy are jumbled

explanation.surface: A shy Jane, coy at heart, has no name of her own and is given one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' leaves JE, and 'Awfully' makes OYC, which 'at heart' sets in the middle. James Joyce wrote Ulysses, the next answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Joyce is a name, a first name and the surname of the novelist James Joyce.

clue.text: Turn with snake in the grass

parts.note: a snake in the grass is a treacherous person, as is a heel, an old word for a cad

explanation.surface: A snake twists and turns as it moves through the grass.
explanation.definitionFit: To wheel is to turn round, as a flock of birds or a line of soldiers wheels.

clue.text: Confined section of the theatre gripped by Bottom

indicators.note: one piece held tight inside another is gripped by it

parts.note: the end of something is its bottom part
the circle is a tier of seats in a theatre, above the stalls

explanation.surface: A seat in the theatre taken over by Bottom, the comic weaver in A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gripped by' signals the container. Bottom in the surface is the weaver in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream; here it simply means the lowest part.
explanation.definitionFit: To be encircled is to be surrounded on all sides, and so hemmed in and confined.

clue.text: Grant the ex-president less latitude stifling last vestige of democracy in America?

indicators.note: the inner letters are placed in the two letters for America

parts.note: US, the United States, stands for America

indicators.note: the mixed-up letters close round and smother one letter
latitude means freedom, so the letters of less are given free rein to move
the last vestige of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A remark that ex-president Grant allowed less freedom, smothering what was left of American democracy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'latitude' (freedom) makes LSSE; 'stifling' wraps it round Y from 'last vestige of' democracy, giving LYSSE, which 'in' places within America's two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulysses S. Grant was the Union general who became the eighteenth president of the United States.

clue.text: Pushy string player's action, having finished with acknowledgement of applause?

parts.note: time is up when it is finished
a performer bows to acknowledge applause

explanation.surface: A violinist at the end of a concert, done playing and bowing to the applause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pushy' is literal: on a stringed instrument the bow is pushed across the strings for an up-bow.
explanation.definitionFit: An up-bow is the stroke in which a string player pushes the bow from tip to heel.

clue.text: See 24
Supposedly released by burning local firewood, oxygen entering isn't freed

parts.note: a local is a pub, and PH is the abbreviation for public house on maps
a log is a piece of firewood

indicators.note: the gas symbol goes in among the freed letters
letters that are freed are let loose to fall in a new order

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Burning firewood at the local pub, with oxygen getting in but nothing being freed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freed' makes ISTN, and 'entering' puts the gas symbol into it, giving ISTON. Phlogiston theory was overturned by Lavoisier's work on oxygen, a nice touch in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Phlogiston was the substance that eighteenth-century chemists wrongly believed was given off when things burned.

clue.text: US state accepted by Red Cross

indicators.note: the state is taken in, accepted inside, the colour

parts.note: IL is the postal abbreviation for Illinois

explanation.surface: A US state taking part in a Red Cross relief scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like part of Red Cross, the charity; it is the definition, meaning angry.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is cross is angry, and someone riled has been made angry.

clue.text: A second city gets senior to cut beastly sound

indicators.note: the abbreviation cuts into the bleat, splitting it

parts.note: baa is the bleat of a sheep, a sound made by a beast

explanation.surface: Another city is given a senior figure to cut down on the noise of animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cut' signals the insertion. 'A second city' reads like 'another city', but it is the definition: Basra is Iraq's second city.
explanation.definitionFit: Basra, the port in southern Iraq, is often called that country's second city.

clue.text: Entry to motorway displays "northbound alternative lager" publicity

indicators.note: in a down clue going north means reading upwards, so both words are read backwards

parts.note: or introduces an alternative
pils is short for Pilsner, a pale lager
an ad, an advertisement, is publicity

explanation.surface: A motorway entry sign shows an advertisement for a different lager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'northbound' turns OR PILS into SLIPRO, ahead of AD.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip road is the short road leading on to or off a motorway.

clue.text: Book setter having day off

indicators.note: the letter for day being off means it is taken away

parts.note: Shed is the pen name of a Guardian crossword setter

explanation.surface: A book by a crossword setter who is taking the day off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' takes D from SHED, a fellow Guardian setter. She is the novel by H. Rider Haggard, part of the puzzle's author theme.
explanation.definitionFit: She is the adventure novel by H. Rider Haggard, about the immortal queen Ayesha.

clue.text: Moving jet-like over a road that's dry

indicators.note: the jet's word goes over the other letters, covering them on both sides

parts.note: sonic speed is the speed of sound, as a jet may fly

explanation.surface: A jet flying over a road in hot, dry country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' signals the container. 'dry' sounds like a weather word; it is the definition, as in dry humour.
explanation.definitionFit: Sardonic humour is grimly mocking, and dry wit is delivered in a similar deadpan, cutting way.

clue.text: Steadfast as a king changing sides at the start

indicators.note: the first letter, R for right, is swapped for L for left, changing sides

parts.note: royal means like or befitting a king

explanation.surface: A loyal follower stands firm, like a king switching allegiance at the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing sides at the start' swaps the first letter of ROYAL, R for right, for L for left.
explanation.definitionFit: A loyal friend is steadfast, firmly faithful and true.

clue.text: A tiny amount for meringue maker?

definitions.meaning: as in winning by a ..., the narrowest margin
a whisk, read playfully as one who whisks egg whites into meringue

explanation.definitionFit: A whisker is a tiny margin, and someone who whisks eggs for meringue could jokingly be called one.

clue.text: Tough, having to accept gag cracking when run down

indicators.note: the tough word takes the scrambled letters inside it

parts.note: hard means tough

indicators.note: something cracking breaks apart, so the letters of gag are broken up and reset

explanation.surface: A tough comic having to put up with a joke falling flat when they are worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracking' makes GGA and 'to accept' signals the container. H. Rider Haggard wrote She, another answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone haggard looks worn and exhausted, as anyone run down does.

clue.text: Trouble when Hardy grabs "smalls"

indicators.note: the outer word grabs the pair of letters and holds them inside

parts.note: hale means healthy and hardy
S is the clothing size small, so two of them are SS

explanation.surface: Thomas Hardy, or a hardy person, snatching someone's underwear, smalls being British slang for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardy' looks like the novelist but it is just healthy; 'smalls' is British slang for underwear, here two small sizes.
explanation.definitionFit: Hassle is trouble or bother, as in all the hassle of moving house.

clue.text: Sharpness of mind very lacking in emptiness

indicators.note: the empty word is lacking the letter for very, which is removed

parts.note: vacuity means emptiness, especially of mind

explanation.surface: A remark that a sharp mind is not found in an empty head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' removes V from VACUITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Acuity is keenness, sharpness of thought or of the senses.

clue.text: Whitehall's "CID-proof" — or worse — corrupt source of rumours

indicators.note: corrupt means spoiled or debased, so these letters are twisted out of shape
the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Whitehall is said to be untouchable by police detectives, or worse, a crooked source of gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrupt' rearranges CID-PROOF OR WORSE, and 'source of' adds R from rumours. Whitehall is the London street of government offices; the phrase is the title of a C. P. Snow novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Whitehall, home of the British civil service, stands for the inner places where government power is exercised.

clue.text: See 8
Trace a lover of Zeus, thanks

parts.note: Io was a mortal woman loved by Zeus in Greek myth, turned into a heifer
ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: A hunt for any trace of one of Zeus's lovers, with a word of thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: An iota is a tiny amount, the smallest trace, from the smallest Greek letter.

clue.text: Contemptible sort of king interrupting Louis XIV, briefly

indicators.note: the single letter breaks into the shortened title
briefly means the title is cut short, losing its ending

parts.note: Louis XIV of France was called the Sun King
K is the abbreviation for king in chess

explanation.surface: A despicable type of monarch breaking in on Louis XIV, the French king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts SUN KING to SUNK, and 'interrupting' puts K inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a skunk brands them a despicable, contemptible person.

clue.text: Stock sum of money that may well be checked

parts.note: stock means lineage or family, as does kin
G is a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: A stock sum of money that is likely to be audited.
explanation.walkthrough: In chess the king is the piece that is put in check. Stephen King wrote Misery, another answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess the king is the piece that is checked, threatened with capture.

clue.text: A chief of police, breaking restriction, performed a caper

indicators.note: the letters break into the restriction, splitting it

parts.note: let is an old word for a hindrance, as in without let or hindrance

indicators.note: the chief of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A police chief breaking the rules and taking part in a criminal caper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' puts A and P, from 'chief of' police, inside LET.
explanation.definitionFit: To leap is to jump or caper, so having leapt is having performed a jump.

clue.text: Some think the Elgin Marbles were long involved with title

definitions.text: Some think the Elgin Marbles were

indicators.note: involved means tangled, so the letters of the two words are mixed together

explanation.surface: A view on the Elgin Marbles, whose long claim to rightful title is disputed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges LONG and TITLE. The Elgin Marbles are classical Greek sculptures taken from the Parthenon to Britain by Lord Elgin.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who want the sculptures returned to Greece say they were acquired dishonestly, which is what ill-gotten means.
